executiveSummary: The OT/ICS threat picture remains elevated. Multiple government advisories confirm active targeting of industrial controllers and exposed OT access paths. Concurrently, new critical vulnerabilities in OT gateways, fuel management, EV charging, and OPC UA stacks increase the likelihood of disruption if left unaddressed. Active, attributed intrusions against PLCs in U.S. water, energy, and municipal environments: actors accessed Rockwell, Siemens, and Schneider controllers over EtherNet/IP, S7, Modbus/TCP, and SSH; observed logic manipulation, alarm suppression, and loss of view. Immediate removal of internet exposure and validation of project integrity are required. Security Advisory Ongoing probing and AI-assisted development of tooling against Siemens S7-200/300/400/1200/1500 PLCs over TCP/102 (S7comm). Harden protection levels, disable PUT/GET where not required, and monitor for anomalous writes. Security Advisory Nation-state operators leveraging large covert networks of compromised SOHO routers/IoT devices as proxy infrastructure to pre-position in critical infrastructure-hardening edge gear and segmentation are urgent priorities. Security Advisory Supply chain and perimeter risk: backdoors found in widely resold ZBT OEM LTE/5G routers (unauthenticated root command execution; active C2) used at the industrial edge. Replace/segregate immediately and block listed C2/ports. View Article New/high-risk OT advisories: - Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced (Node-RED HTTP interface unauthenticated RCE; CVSS 10) - patch to V4.3.4.1, disable or secure Node-RED; - All-Line Fuel-Boss V1 (PHP IMAP and PHP-FPM issues enabling RCE) - remove internet exposure and apply vendor fixes. Security Advisory Security Advisory OT/adjacent vulnerability surge: - EVSE ecosystems (Autel, EVbee) with unauthenticated remote RCE and weak update controls; - OPC UA (Eclipse Milo) method/diag bypass and DoS issues affecting ICS servers; - Water smart-meter management (Baylan BMS) missing auth on critical functions. Bulletin Bulletin Bulletin Enterprise-to-OT pivot risks remain significant: Zimbra zero-days used for bulk email theft, SonicWall SMA exploitation, and TrueConf supply-chain delivery of backdoors raise lateral-movement risk toward OT segments when segmentation is weak. items: Iranian-affiliated actors: direct PLC access, project exfiltration, and logic/alarm modifications in U.S. CI sectors. Security Advisory
PRC nexus: covert SOHO/IoT proxy botnets to pre-position within CI; separate advisory details long-term telecom/router compromise TTPs. Security Advisory Security Advisory
Pro-Russia hacktivists: opportunistic HMI/VNC compromises (ports 5900-5910), setpoint changes, operator lockout; confirmed operational disruption. Security Advisory
APT "Head Mare": exploiting TrueConf server zero-days to deliver backdoors (supply-chain risk to partners/vendors). Supporting Report
QTFY (PRC-linked): custom platforms and VPN exploits against U.S. government and CI; hardened VPN and IoT edges advised. View Article

relevance: Direct OT impact is confirmed in multiple advisories and reports: adversary access to PLCs and HMIs (logic/alarm tampering), critical RCEs on OT gateways (SIMATIC IoT2050), EV charging/CSMS ecosystems (Autel/EVbee), and OPC UA stack weaknesses (Eclipse Milo) affecting industrial servers. Most affected technologies: PLCs (Rockwell, Siemens, Schneider), HMIs (VNC-exposed), industrial gateways/IIoT (SIMATIC IoT2050), OPC UA servers, fuel/dispensing control, EVSE, and smart metering backends. Primary exposure paths: direct internet access to OT assets, weak edge device configurations (routers/VPNs), compromised remote-access appliances, and IT-OT pivots following enterprise email/VPN breaches.

items: Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced: Node-RED unauthenticated RCE (CVSS 10) - update to V4.3.4.1; require adminAuth/TLS; isolate editor endpoints. Security Advisory
All-Line Fuel-Boss V1: PHP IMAP injection and PHP-FPM buffer overwrite leading to RCE; remove internet exposure and apply vendor fixes. Security Advisory
Eclipse Milo (OPC UA): method/diag bypass, token padding oracle, chunk/monitored-item DoS - upgrade Milo-based components; enforce strong security policies. Bulletin
EV charging (Autel/EVbee): unauthenticated WebSocket/OCPP RCE paths and weak update/auth - segment EVSE, enforce mTLS pinning, lock ports, and patch. Bulletin Bulletin
Baylan Smart Meter Management: missing authentication on critical functions - restrict access, update to v1.1.10.142+. Bulletin
DAQFactory (SCADA/HMI) and ibaPDA: file/deserialize-driven RCE on engineering/data collection hosts - restrict untrusted files, apply vendor updates. Bulletin Bulletin

descriptions: Initial access: exploitation of internet-exposed PLCs/HMIs (S7comm TCP/102; Modbus/TCP 502; EtherNet/IP 44818/2222), exposed VNC (5900-5910), vulnerable routers/VPNs (SNMP/SMI/SSL VPN).
Persistence: rogue accounts on appliances; web shells; modified Node-RED flows; IMAP app passwords; router config implants.
Privilege escalation & lateral movement: credential harvesting (Kerberos/NTLM via compromised perimeter devices), Impacket tools, reverse tunnels.
Impact (ICS ATT&CK): Modify Controller Logic (T0831), Alarm Suppression (T0826), Loss of View (T0827), Unauthorized Command/Message (T0858).

outlook72h: Run an external exposure sweep: confirm no PLC/HMI ports (102/502/44818/2222/5900-5910) are internet-reachable; immediately remediate any findings. Emergency change window: update Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 to V4.3.4.1+; remove/lock Node-RED editor; apply Fuel-Boss fixes; upgrade Milo-based services. Edge lockdown: SNMPv3-migrate and disable SMI; remove WAN management; rotate router/VPN credentials; geofence admin access. EVSE segmentation: isolate chargers from enterprise; require mTLS to CSMS; disable unused local interfaces (USB/NFC/Bluetooth) where feasible. Validate controller integrity: compare PLC logic to golden baselines; re-enable/verify alarms; set physical keyswitch to RUN where applicable.
